title: Arsenal vs. Man City, a Spygate rematch, Verón, Madrid, and more
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: HomePostsArsenal vs. Man City, a Spygate rematch, Verón, Madrid, and moreArsenal vs. Man City, a Spygate rematch, Verón, Madrid, and moreThere's extra spice everywhere you look in club football this weekend
Juan Sebastián Verón’s father won the Copa Libertadores three years running with Estudiantes. On Saturday, Verón is chasing a fifth title for the club as its president.
Elsewhere, Arsenal host Manchester City, Everton face Liverpool, Middlesbrough visit Southampton in a Spygate rematch, and the Allsvenskan title goes to the final day.

Arsenal vs. Manchester City is this weekend’s obvious headlinerThe defending champions play at home against the side who’ve dominated the Premier League for so much of the last decade: it doesn’t get much bigger than this. Arsenal come into the game with a six-point lead over chasers Brighton and Man City, with City currently on a four-game winless run in league play.
Arsenal have an impressive six-point lead with 11 rounds played in the Premier League
In a further contrast, the Gunners are unbeaten in 11, and having won all five of their games at the Emirates, are the only side in the division not to have dropped a single point at home.

Viktor Gyökeres, Arsenal’s scorer in the Champions League in midweek, has 17 goals in 2026. City’s Erling Haaland is one of only two players based in the Premier League with more during this calendar year. The Norwegian has 27 in total, but none in his last three.
A break in that dry spell will surely have a massive impact on Sunday’s game.
🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🔮 This weekend’s Premier League predictions from the Opta Supercomputer

Everton and Liverpool have been going at it since 1894, with this being the oldest top-flight derby in English football. Sunday’s game, however, will only be the second played at Everton’s new home, the Hill Dickinson.
Evertonians won’t want to be reminded of the first, when Virgil van Dijk popped up in the 10th minute of added time to steal all three points in the corresponding fixture last season.
Both Everton and Liverpool have an in-form striker heading into the derby

David Moyes broke a club record for most games managed at Everton in Monday’s disappointing defeat at Brentford. Whether he’ll get anything from his upcoming 594th game in charge will likely depend on the form of Thierno Barry, who’s scored five and assisted another of Everton's last seven league goals.
Liverpool have some form players of their own: Alexander Isak has four in his last four games, and Florian Wirtz has six in five for club and country.
🤬🟥 Did you know that Everton vs. Liverpool has produced the most red cards in the Premier League era?

José Mourinho is a happy man at the moment. His Real Madrid side have won each of their last 10 games, including this week’s comeback against PSV, a result that keeps them perfect and top of the league phase table in the Champions League.

Kylian Mbappé has 19 goals in 18 appearances so far this campaign, and in Jude Bellingham, Mourinho believes he has “the best midfielder in the world.” The only sticking point might be that Barcelona are still three points ahead of Madrid at the top of LaLiga.
It’s all coming up green for José Mourinho at the moment

Spain’s big two rarely play on the same day, so each round becomes a game of cat and mouse. Madrid host Deportivo Alavés on Saturday evening and have beaten them in all of their previous nine meetings. A win would close the gap for a few hours, at least until Barcelona visit Deportivo A Coruña on Sunday.
🇪🇸🏆 After two trophy-less seasons Real Madrid are contenders once more
